title: Ankle Sprain or Fracture? How to Tell the Difference
metaDescription: Twisted your ankle? Learn the signs that separate a simple sprain from a fracture, correct first aid, and when an X-ray is essential — from a foot & ankle surgeon in Thane.
intro: Most twisted ankles are ligament sprains that heal with simple care. But some are fractures or significant ligament ruptures, and treating these like a minor sprain leads to chronic pain and instability.

sections.heading: Signs that suggest a fracture
bullets: Inability to take four steps immediately after injury or in the clinic
Bone tenderness over the ankle prominences (malleoli) or midfoot
Rapid, severe swelling with visible deformity
Numbness or color change in the foot

sections.heading: Sprain or fracture: how the two compare
sections.body: No table replaces an examination, and severe sprains can look every bit as dramatic as fractures. Use this to judge how urgently you need assessment, not to rule a fracture out.

table.caption: General patterns only — an X-ray is the reliable way to distinguish the two.
rows: Soft tissue just below or in front of the ankle bone
Directly over the bone, on the back edge or tip of either ankle bone
Painful but usually possible, often with a limp
Often impossible to take four steps, immediately and afterwards
Often none, sometimes a tearing sensation
A crack or snap is sometimes reported
Rapid and severe, sometimes with visible deformity
Visible deformity or the foot pointing abnormally
Needs urgent assessment — may indicate nerve or vessel involvement
Immobilisation, and surgery if fragments are displaced or the joint is involved

sections.heading: Correct first aid
sections.body: Follow RICE — Rest, Ice (15–20 minutes at a time), Compression bandage and Elevation above heart level. Avoid massage, hot fomentation and walking through severe pain in the first 48 hours.

sections.heading: Why proper assessment matters
sections.body: Repeated "minor" sprains often mean an untreated ligament injury. Chronic ankle instability is preventable with early physiotherapy, bracing, and in selected cases arthroscopic ligament repair. A weight-bearing X-ray decides the matter in minutes.

faqs.q: Can I walk on a fractured ankle?
faqs.a: Sometimes, yes — which is why "I can walk, so it is not broken" is unreliable. Undisplaced fractures may allow painful walking but still need protection to heal correctly.

faqs.q: How long does an ankle sprain take to heal?
faqs.a: Mild sprains settle in 1–3 weeks; moderate ones in 4–6 weeks. Pain beyond 6 weeks deserves specialist review for ligament or cartilage injury.

faqs.q: Do all ankle fractures need surgery?
faqs.a: No. Stable, well-aligned fractures heal in a cast or boot. Surgery is needed when the joint surface is displaced or the ankle is unstable.
